title: Judge with atomic yes/no questions, not one overall mark
rule: Ask the judge a list of small, separate checks (right kind of being, right clothes, right place, right count) and combine them yourself.
why: Question-and-answer scoring is more explainable and more reliable than one holistic score, but only if each question is atomic and non-overlapping.
how: Write one check per fact in the brief; ask for what is seen first, then match. Example: "Mimi wears X: yes or no".

monofilm.idea: Make the clip review answer a fixed checklist per scene fact too, not only free issues.

title: Give the judge the approved reference as ground truth
rule: Send the approved reference pictures with the picture or frames being judged and tell the judge to compare against them, not against the words.
why: Pair comparison is where multimodal judges are closest to humans; scoring a single item alone drifts from human preference.
how: "Judge identity against the START and END pictures, never the written description."

monofilm.where: src/picturecheck.js refs (up to 3); src/takereview.js pictures (start and end)

title: Do not trust a vision judge on counts and tiny details
rule: Treat "how many", small accessories and overlapping objects as unreliable verdicts: confirm them another way or let the human decide.
why: Simple counting and overlap tasks drew only 58% from top vision models, and accuracy fell when objects touched.
how: Keep kind "detail" and "count" as minor (do not hard-stop); put the count in the prompt as a fact; for a count that matters crop and ask one question on the crop.

monofilm.where: src/picturecheck.js: kind detail is not major; src/takereview.js: count issues give advice only
monofilm.idea: Crop-and-recheck step for counts; show these verdicts to the human as "unsure".

title: Look a second time before failing a picture
rule: When a picture fails the check, run the check once more and only count it failed if it fails twice.
why: Judges are inconsistent (they contradict themselves and vary run to run), so one negative look wastes a good picture.
how: Second look uses the same checklist; mark it secondOpinion so the page can say so.

monofilm.idea: Apply the same two-look rule to a failed clip review before burning a retry.

title: Judge clips from several frames in time order
rule: Send the judge 6 to 8 frames in order, plus start and end pictures, and ask what changes between frames.
why: Count, shape and place changes only show across frames; a single frame cannot reveal them. Physical consistency is its own scored dimension.
how: Frames evenly spaced, numbered; ask for the frame range of each fault.

title: Score quality, prompt match and physics separately
rule: Keep visual quality, match to the brief and physical sense as separate verdicts so a retry targets the right fault.
why: Reward models and benchmarks score these dimensions apart because a clip can look beautiful and still break physics.
how: issues carry a kind (count, physics, jump, identity, state); route advice by kind.

monofilm.idea: Add a separate plain "looks good" mark so beauty is not mixed with correctness.

title: Cap retries and hand over to the human
rule: Allow at most about three takes per clip, change the seed each time, then stop and tell the person.
why: Loops need a stopping rule; repeating a failing prompt rarely helps without new information.
how: Deterministic seed per scene, clip and attempt; after the cap say "change the brief".

title: Feed the critic's concrete advice back into the next prompt
rule: Turn each detected fault into one plain sentence of what must be true and add it to the next prompt.
why: Critic-to-rewriter loops (a reasoning step that rewrites the prompt from critiques) won up to 60% of pairwise comparisons; a bare retry has nothing new.
how: "The bottle is open, with its cap off, the whole time." State the wanted state, not the fault.

title: Critique must use a signal other than the generator's opinion
rule: Combine the model judge with measured checks (frozen tail, cuts, jumps) and the human's approvals.
why: Models asked to fix themselves with no external feedback often do not improve and can get worse.
how: Measured hold, smooth and cut counts sit beside the vision verdict and both go into advice.

monofilm.idea: Judge with a different model than the one that drew the picture, to reduce self-preference.

title: Make several candidates and let a verifier pick (best-of-N)
rule: For a costly or failure-prone shot, generate two to four candidates and keep the one the verifier ranks highest.
why: More candidates scored by a verifier raised video quality steadily; reward models for video are built for this.
how: Rank by the checklist result first, measured flaws second, human choice last.

monofilm.where: Faces are drawn as lettered candidates (src/wizard.js makeFace); clips are retried one at a time
monofilm.idea: Auto-rank parallel clip takes with reviewFrames before showing them.

title: Repair the failed part, keep the good part
rule: Regenerate only the clip or region that failed and keep everything else the person approved.
why: Localised repair kept correct regions and beat full regeneration on two benchmarks.
how: Per-clip retries, never a whole-scene redo; keep approved frames fixed.

monofilm.where: Clips are retried individually (retryAdvice per scene and clip)

title: A prompt rewriter must keep the person's intent
rule: After any automatic rewrite, check that the facts of the brief survived and nothing unsafe or new was added.
why: Generic LLM rewriting can distort intent, drop key details and add risk; good rewriters are trained on harmless, accurate and helpful goals.
how: Compare rewritten facts with the original list (who, where, count, action); reject a rewrite that drops one.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js text() clamps; reviewContinuity edits states and moves
monofilm.idea: Add a diff check that names are all still present after a rewrite.

title: Rewrite for the target model, with its own dialect
rule: Tune the rewrite to the one video model in use, not to video models in general.
why: A rewriter that ignores which model runs the prompt gains less; model-aware rewriting is the point of Prompt-A-Video.
how: Keep a per-model prompt profile and apply it in the last step.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js clip prompts are written for Meta; no per-model profile
monofilm.idea: Per-model profile in the knowledge base models/ notes, read by the prompt composer.

title: Let a director step plan, a critic step check, but ground it
rule: In a planner and critic pipeline, give the critic the concrete state (story, references) and a checklist, and measure the benefit.
why: Multi-agent film pipelines report gains (FilmAgent beat a single stronger model), but they are small studies on virtual 3D scenes or rating by few people.
how: One continuity review pass over the whole scene list before any picture is spent.

title: Keep people in the loop at checkpoints
rule: Stop for human approval before the costly steps and at any blocker, and record who approved.
why: Agent systems should pause for human feedback at checkpoints and have a hard iteration cap.
how: Faces, places, scenes approved before frames; autopilot stops on a stuck step and on no credits.

monofilm.where: src/autopilot.js (approvals recorded as "Approved by Roll camera", stuck and budget stops)

title: When the filter blocks a harmless prompt, change the prompt, not the dice
rule: On a content-filter refusal, rewrite the prompt (drop the negative clause, shorten sentences, swap trigger words) instead of retrying the same text.
why: Over-refusal is a known trade-off of safety filters; users report the prompt and the output frames are both screened, so identical retries fail again.
how: Order: drop "never show" lists, then shorten each sentence, then replace violent or child words with neutral ones, then ask the person.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js drawChecked (retry without the never-show clause, then cut sentences at first comma)
monofilm.idea: Same retry ladder for video clips, and one for a refused image-to-video start frame.

title: Find the trigger by cutting down, then adding back
rule: If rewriting does not help, strip the prompt to its core and add parts back one at a time until the block returns.
why: A bisect finds the word; guessing does not. Also test with prompt enhancement off, since it can add flagged words.
how: Keep a log of blocked phrases per model in the knowledge base.

monofilm.idea: Add the bisect ladder and a blocked-phrase log per model.

title: Check the input pictures when image-to-video is blocked
rule: If a clip with a start or end frame is refused, suspect the picture (logo, face like a known person, skin) before the words.
why: The filter screens pictures as well as text; third-party people and brands have their own block categories.
how: Redraw the frame without the logo or crop it; use invented faces only.

monofilm.idea: Detect a refusal on a frame and redraw that frame with a different pose or crop.

title: Do not depict real people or famous characters
rule: Use only invented characters and places; never ask for a real person, a celebrity or a studio's characters.
why: Providers block celebrity and third-party content and require consent for likeness; studios have sued over lookalike characters.
how: Character briefs describe an invented design, not "in the style of" a named franchise.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js lookText filters risky "never show" words; characters are invented from the story
monofilm.idea: Warn when a character name matches a known franchise or public figure.

title: Keep children out unless the tool allows it, and phrase neutrally
rule: Expect the video model to block depicted children by default; plan characters as animals or stylised figures, or use the neutral word the provider accepts.
why: Veo rejects child depictions unless a setting allows it, and minors get tighter moderation on Sora.
how: Animal or toy characters; "young person" instead of "child" where a person is needed, within the provider rules.

monofilm.where: Studio films use animal characters in tests; no rule written
monofilm.idea: Add the rule to the scene writer with a clear note to the person.

title: Set the made-for-kids flag and know COPPA when the film is for children
rule: If the audience is children, mark the upload made-for-kids and avoid collecting data; animation alone does not decide it.
why: YouTube needs the setting per video; the FTC weighs animated characters, music, ages and audience together.
how: Show a reminder on the ship page for kids' films.

monofilm.idea: Ship page question "Is this made for children?" with the consequences.

title: Disclose realistic synthetic content when publishing
rule: Tick the platform's AI disclosure for realistic-looking AI video; clearly unrealistic or animated work is exempt, but disclosing is safe.
why: YouTube requires it for realistic content and can penalise repeated omissions; Meta labels from file signals and self-disclosure; the EU AI Act asks for machine-readable marking from August 2026.
how: Ship page text: what to tick on YouTube, TikTok and Meta.

monofilm.idea: Add a ship checklist with platform disclosure steps.

title: Keep provenance marks; do not strip them
rule: Keep any C2PA manifest or invisible watermark the generator adds, and add a content credential on export where possible.
why: Manifests can be stripped by re-encoding, so a soft binding (watermark or fingerprint) is the way back; SynthID is built to survive crops, filters and compression.
how: Prefer stream copy or tools that keep metadata; record the maker and edit steps.

monofilm.idea: Export step that preserves or writes a C2PA manifest and notes the generator.

title: Keep a record of human choices to support authorship
rule: Record the person's own selections, edits and arrangement of the generated material.
why: The US Copyright Office says prompts alone do not make the user the author, while creative selection, arrangement and modification can be protected.
how: Store the approvals, the picked takes and the edit order with timestamps.

monofilm.where: Approvals and picked takes are recorded under the person's name (src/autopilot.js, store)
monofilm.idea: Export a "human contribution" log from the project history.
